**Date:** ___ May 2026  

**Muhammad Akbar Mahar**  
Commissioner Inland Revenue,  
Zone-VI, Large Taxpayers’ Office,  
Karachi.  

**Subject: Reply to Show Cause Notice C.No. CIR/Zone-VI/Suspension-ST/LTO/Khi/2025-26/348 dated 21 May 2026 issued under Section 21(2A) of the Sales Tax Act, 1990 read with Rule 12(a)(vi) of the Sales Tax Rules, 2006 — Proposed Blacklisting**

Dear Sir,  

We refer to the above-mentioned show cause notice dated **21 May 2026** whereby K-Electric Limited [the “Company”] has been called upon to show cause as to why it may not be blacklisted under section 21(2A) of the Sales Tax Act, 1990 read with Rule 12(a)(vi) of the Sales Tax Rules, 2006, allegedly on account of non-compliance with S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 dated 21 March 2023.

At the outset, the Company respectfully denies the allegations contained in the impugned notice. The notice proceeds on materially incorrect assumptions, overlooks prior compliance already made by the Company, and seeks to invoke the extreme and stigmatic consequence of blacklisting without first establishing any deliberate suppression, false declaration, misstatement, or tax fraud within the meaning of the Sales Tax Act, 1990.

### 1. The impugned notice materially changes the basis of allegation from the earlier suspension proceedings

The present notice appears to have been issued in continuation of the earlier proceedings initiated through Show Cause Notice No. **CIR/Zone-VI/LTO/Khi/2025-26/341 dated 19 May 2026**, whereby the Company was called upon to explain why its sales tax registration should not be suspended under section 21(2) of the Sales Tax Act, 1990 read with Rule 12 of the Sales Tax Rules, 2006.

It is respectfully submitted that the earlier notice was premised mainly on an alleged decline in recovery ratio from **92.2%** for the period **June 2024 to February 2025** to **89.6%** for the period **June 2025 to February 2026**. On that basis, the department alleged that the recoveries declared by the Company were not verifiable and that there was supposed suppression of output tax.

In contrast, the present blacklisting notice has completely altered the scope and basis of allegation. Instead of relying on the same limited comparative recovery-ratio analysis, the present notice extends the period to **February 2023 to March 2026** and alleges that against total output sales tax billed of **Rs. 326,567,252,303**, the Company declared collection of **Rs. 289,041,889,607**. This is a new allegation, covering a substantially wider period and a different factual basis.

It is therefore respectfully submitted that proceedings for blacklisting cannot validly be founded upon a suspension exercise where the original show-cause was based on an entirely different observation, different period, and different working. The Company cannot be penalized on the basis of shifting allegations unless a proper, specific, period-wise, transaction-wise, and legally sustainable basis is first provided and adequate opportunity is afforded to rebut the same.

### 2. Prior compliance already made for February 2023 to May 2025 has been completely ignored

The allegation that the Company failed to comply with S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 or failed to furnish requisite information is contrary to the record.

In this regard, reference is invited to letter bearing reference **DST-1806 dated 17 June 2025**, submitted through the Company’s authorized representative in response to notice No. **DCIR/U-4/Z-VI/LTO/S-147/2024-25/e-dox-11588 dated 10 June 2025**. Through the said letter, the Company had already furnished information pertaining to the overall movement, including recoveries and defaulting consumers, for the tax periods **February 2023 to May 2025** as **Annexure ‘A’**.

Accordingly, a major portion of the very period now referred to in the impugned blacklisting notice had already been responded to and the relevant data had already been submitted before the department. The present notice, however, proceeds as if no compliance was ever made. This assumption is factually incorrect and has resulted in an erroneous and unjustified escalation of the matter.

A copy of the aforesaid letter dated **17 June 2025**, along with acknowledgment, is enclosed herewith for ready reference as **Annexure ‘A’**.

### 3. The Company has been declaring available information in the sales tax return within the limitations of IRIS

It is further submitted that the Company has been duly declaring the requisite information in the relevant tab/annexure of the monthly sales tax return to the extent permitted by the IRIS portal.

As already explained in the Company’s earlier correspondence, the IRIS portal provides only pre-defined fields for reporting relevant information. There is no independent system-based facility in the monthly sales tax return enabling a DISCO to upload detailed consumer-wise, party-wise, or structured defaulting-consumer data beyond the fields made available by FBR. A taxpayer cannot be expected to upload or declare information in a format that the system itself does not permit.

This important limitation was specifically highlighted to the department earlier. Despite the same, the present notice seeks to shift the entire burden of system limitation upon the taxpayer and treats the matter as non-compliance. Such an approach is neither fair nor legally sustainable, particularly where the Company had, without prejudice and in good faith, already provided relevant data manually when called upon to do so.

### 4. Difference between billed sales tax and recovered sales tax does not constitute tax fraud

The central assumption in the impugned notice appears to be that the difference between output sales tax billed and output sales tax recovered represents suppression or short declaration of tax liability. This assumption is fundamentally misconceived in the context of S.R.O. 376(I)/2023.

S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 prescribes a special procedure for collection and payment of sales tax on electric power supplied by DISCOs. The framework itself recognizes the practical distinction between tax billed through electricity bills and tax actually recovered from consumers. In the electricity distribution sector, billing and recovery do not always occur in the same tax period. Recoveries are affected by delayed payments, instalments, government receivables, consumer category, disputed bills, operational constraints, and defaulting consumers.

Therefore, an unrecovered portion of billed sales tax cannot automatically be equated with suppression of output tax. At best, the issue requires reconciliation between billed amounts, recovered amounts, unpaid amounts, and amounts reported under the relevant return annexures. Such reconciliation exercise cannot be converted into an allegation of tax fraud without identifying specific false declarations, concealed recoveries, fake entries, or deliberate withholding of tax actually recovered from consumers.

The impugned notice does not identify any specific transaction, consumer, return entry, recovery receipt, or payment record showing that tax recovered by the Company was not deposited. In the absence of such evidence, the allegation of tax fraud is premature, excessive, and unsustainable.

### 5. No basis or working of the alleged figures has been provided

The impugned notice refers to total output sales tax billed of **Rs. 326,567,252,303** and declared collection of **Rs. 289,041,889,607** for the period **February 2023 to March 2026**. However, no supporting working has been provided to explain how these figures have been computed.

In particular, the notice does not provide:

- tax-period-wise breakup of the alleged billed and recovered sales tax;
- consumer category-wise reconciliation;
- mapping with monthly sales tax returns;
- reference to specific return annexures relied upon by the department;
- details of any alleged unreconciled or suppressed recovery;
- identification of any tax amount actually recovered but not deposited; or
- basis for treating unrecovered billed tax as tax fraud.

In the absence of such working, the Company is unable to meaningfully respond to the computation underlying the allegation. It is respectfully requested that if the department maintains any such position, complete working and underlying basis may first be provided so that the Company may examine and respond to the same in a proper manner.

### 6. Earlier opportunity was wholly inadequate and proceedings were escalated mechanically

The earlier notice dated **19 May 2026** fixed the hearing on **20 May 2026**, i.e. on the very next day of issuance. The notice required reconciliation of voluminous data covering multiple tax periods. The Company responded through letter dated **21 May 2026**, explaining that such extensive reconciliation could not reasonably be compiled within one day and requested withdrawal of the proceedings or grant of reasonable time.

Despite the said response, the matter appears to have been escalated to suspension and thereafter to blacklisting without meaningful consideration of the Company’s explanation. This sequence is inconsistent with the principles of natural justice and with FBR’s own instructions issued vide C.No.6(4)Rev.Bud/2018 dated 23 July 2018, wherein field formations were directed to allow sufficient time/fair opportunity of at least fifteen days after receipt of notice for necessary compliance.

The Company is one of the largest regulated taxpayers and contributors to the national exchequer on a monthly basis. Invoking suspension and blacklisting proceedings without allowing reasonable time for reconciliation of complex DISCO data is harsh, disproportionate, and inconsistent with the facilitative approach expected in such matters.

### 7. No case of “persistent violation” or blacklisting is made out

Blacklisting is an extreme measure and cannot be invoked merely because the department requires further reconciliation or further explanation. The Company has neither refused to comply nor withheld any record. On the contrary, the Company has already submitted relevant data earlier for **February 2023 to May 2025**, has been declaring available information in the monthly sales tax returns, and remains willing to provide further reconciliation or clarification as may reasonably be required.

The present matter, at its highest, is a matter of reconciliation under a special procedure applicable to DISCOs. It does not disclose any intentional act of tax fraud, suppression, or persistent non-compliance. In the absence of such essential ingredients, proceedings under section 21(2A) read with Rule 12(a)(vi) are not attracted.

### 8. Position regarding permanent defaulters

As already clarified in earlier correspondence, no consumer presently qualifies as a “permanent defaulter” within the meaning of Rule 6 of S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 unless the cumulative conditions prescribed therein are satisfied, including exhaustion of recovery measures, removal of meter, initiation of legal proceedings, and verification that no other meter is installed or electricity is being supplied at the same premises.

Since no consumer met the complete set of prescribed conditions for classification as a permanent defaulter for the relevant period under review, the requirement for a CEO-countersigned certificate did not arise at that stage. This position was also explained in the earlier compliance submitted through letter dated **17 June 2025**.

### 9. Without prejudice, the Company remains willing to re-submit and reconcile the data

Without prejudice to the legal and factual objections raised above, and without admitting any default, the Company remains committed to full compliance with the provisions of the Sales Tax Act, 1990 and S.R.O. 376(I)/2023.

The Company is willing to re-submit the data already furnished earlier and to provide further reconciliation for the remaining period, if any, in a mutually agreed and workable format. However, the same should not be treated as admission of any non-compliance, particularly when the Company has already complied to the extent permitted by IRIS and has also provided manual data when called upon.

### Prayer

In view of the foregoing submissions, it is respectfully requested that:

1. the impugned show cause notice dated **21 May 2026** issued for proposed blacklisting may kindly be withdrawn;  
2. the allegation of tax fraud and persistent violation may kindly be dropped, being contrary to facts and law;  
3. the suspension proceedings/order referred to in the impugned notice may also be reconsidered/withdrawn, as the matter is purely reconciliatory in nature;  
4. the prior compliance made through letter **DST-1806 dated 17 June 2025** may kindly be taken on record; and  
5. in the alternative, if any further clarification is still required, the department may kindly provide complete period-wise working of the alleged difference and allow reasonable time of at least fifteen days for submission of reconciliation and supporting record.

This reply is submitted without prejudice to any other legal, factual, procedural, or jurisdictional submissions which the Company may raise at any subsequent stage.

Yours faithfully,  

For and on behalf of  
**K-Electric Limited**  

_____________________  
Authorized Signatory  

**Enclosures:**  
1. Copy of letter DST-1806 dated 17 June 2025 along with acknowledgment.  
2. Copy of earlier reply dated 21 May 2026.  
3. Relevant reconciliation/data already submitted earlier, where required.

---

### 4. The difference between billed sales tax and recovered sales tax is not tax fraud

The principal assumption in the impugned notice appears to be that the difference between output sales tax billed and output sales tax recovered represents suppressed output tax. This assumption is legally and factually misconceived in the case of a DISCO operating under S.R.O. 376(I)/2023.

S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 was issued precisely to address the peculiar nature of the electric power distribution sector, where sales tax is billed to consumers through electricity bills, but actual realization depends upon subsequent recovery from consumers. The special procedure recognizes the distinction between billing and recovery and prescribes a mechanism for collection and payment accordingly.

In the electricity distribution sector, recoveries are affected by several factors, including delayed consumer payments, instalment arrangements, disputed bills, government receivables, category-wise consumer behavior, operational constraints, litigation, delayed realization and defaulting consumers. These factors are commercial and regulatory realities of the sector. They cannot be treated as evidence of suppression unless the department identifies a specific amount of tax that was actually recovered from consumers but not deposited by the Company.

The impugned notice does not identify any such amount. It does not point out any specific consumer, bill, receipt, tax period, return entry, bank recovery or collection record showing that sales tax was recovered by the Company but not deposited into the Government treasury. In the absence of such evidence, the difference between billed and recovered sales tax cannot be converted into an allegation of tax fraud.

---

### 5. No working or basis of the alleged figures has been provided

The impugned notice refers to total output sales tax billed of Rs. 326,567,252,303 and declared collection of Rs. 289,041,889,607 for the period February 2023 to March 2026. However, no detailed working, computation or basis has been provided with the notice.

The notice does not provide:

a. tax-period-wise breakup of billed sales tax;  
b. tax-period-wise breakup of recovered sales tax;  
c. reconciliation with monthly sales tax returns;  
d. reference to the specific return annexures relied upon;  
e. consumer category-wise working;  
f. details of unpaid/defaulted amounts considered by the department;  
g. identification of any tax actually recovered but allegedly not deposited;  
h. particulars of any alleged false declaration; or  
i. basis for treating unrecovered billed sales tax as tax fraud.

In the absence of such details, the Company is unable to verify the figures stated in the notice or provide a meaningful reconciliation. The Company respectfully requests that if the department still maintains the above allegation, complete period-wise and annexure-wise working may first be provided so that the Company may examine and respond to the same in an appropriate manner.

---

### 6. Recovery-ratio movement cannot be treated as evidence of suppression

The earlier notice proceeded on the basis that the recovery ratio had declined from 92.2% to 89.6%. This represents a movement of approximately 2.6 percentage points. Such movement, by itself, cannot constitute evidence of suppression, short declaration or tax fraud.

Recovery ratios of a regulated electricity distribution company are influenced by multiple external and operational factors. These include seasonal consumption trends, billing cycles, customer mix, delayed payments, recoveries from government consumers, industrial and commercial demand variation, ageing of receivables, payment plans and delayed realization. These factors require proper examination and reconciliation. They do not justify an automatic presumption that the Company has suppressed output tax.

It is respectfully submitted that the Sales Tax Act, 1990 does not permit the department to presume tax fraud merely on the basis of recovery-ratio movement. A serious allegation such as tax fraud must be based on cogent material and specific evidence. No such evidence has been identified in the impugned notice.

---

### 7. The ingredients for blacklisting under section 21(2A) and Rule 12(a)(vi) are not established

Blacklisting is an extraordinary and highly prejudicial action. It has serious commercial, regulatory and reputational consequences. Such action cannot be invoked merely because a reconciliation is required or because there is a difference between billed and recovered amounts under a special procedure.

The impugned notice alleges persistent violation and tax fraud. However, the essential ingredients of such allegation have not been established. The notice does not demonstrate that the Company has:

a. issued fake or false invoices;  
b. suppressed taxable supplies;  
c. recovered sales tax from consumers and failed to deposit the same;  
d. made false declarations in the sales tax returns;  
e. concealed any material record;  
f. failed to provide information despite reasonable and specific requisition; or  
g. deliberately violated any mandatory requirement of S.R.O. 376(I)/2023.

On the contrary, the record shows that the Company has been filing sales tax returns, reporting available information in the prescribed system fields, depositing recovered sales tax, responding to departmental notices, and furnishing manual data when called upon.

Therefore, the case does not fall within the scope of blacklisting. At most, the matter requires reconciliation of billed, recovered and unpaid amounts under the special procedure. Such reconciliation issue cannot be converted into proceedings for blacklisting.

---

### 8. No adverse inference can be drawn due to system limitations in IRIS

The Company respectfully reiterates that where the IRIS system does not provide a specific facility for uploading detailed party-wise or consumer-wise information in the monthly sales tax return, no adverse inference can be drawn against the taxpayer for not furnishing such data electronically.

The Company has no control over the structure of the return, the design of IRIS, or the fields enabled by FBR. If FBR requires any additional format, structured annexure or separate electronic filing facility for DISCOs under S.R.O. 376(I)/2023, the same may be prescribed and enabled formally. Until such mechanism is available, the taxpayer cannot be treated as non-compliant merely because the system does not allow the desired level of reporting.

This point was already explained in the earlier letter dated 17 June 2025. Despite this, the impugned notice shifts the entire burden of system limitation to the Company, which is neither fair nor sustainable.

---

### 9. Position regarding permanent defaulters under Rule 6

As already clarified in earlier correspondence, no consumer could be classified as a “permanent defaulter” unless all conditions prescribed under Rule 6 of S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 are cumulatively satisfied.

The said conditions include, inter alia, exhaustion of recovery measures, removal of electricity meter, initiation of legal proceedings and verification that no other meter is installed or electricity is being supplied at the same premises. Unless these conditions are fulfilled, a consumer cannot be treated as a permanent defaulter for the purpose of the said rule.

The Company had earlier clarified that, for the period under review, no consumer met the complete set of conditions necessary to be classified as a permanent defaulter. Consequently, the requirement for submission of a CEO-countersigned certificate did not arise at that stage.

This position has already been communicated to the department and cannot be treated as non-compliance.

---

### 10. The proceedings suffer from violation of reasonable opportunity and natural justice

The earlier show-cause notice dated 19 May 2026 fixed hearing on 20 May 2026, i.e. on the very next day of issuance. The notice required reconciliation and explanation of voluminous data relating to multiple tax periods. It was practically impossible for the Company to compile, verify and submit such extensive information within one day.

The Company submitted its response dated 21 May 2026 and specifically highlighted that the opportunity provided was neither meaningful nor reasonable. The Company also referred to FBR’s own instructions issued vide C.No.6(4)Rev.Bud/2018 dated 23 July 2018, which require field formations to allow sufficient time/fair opportunity of at least fifteen days after receipt of notice.

Despite this, the proceedings were escalated to suspension and thereafter to proposed blacklisting. Such escalation, without first considering the Company’s response and without granting reasonable time for reconciliation, is contrary to the principles of natural justice and due process.

---

### 11. The Company is a major compliant taxpayer and the allegation of tax fraud is wholly unwarranted

The Company is one of the largest regulated taxpayers and contributors to the national exchequer. It collects and deposits substantial amounts of sales tax and withholding taxes on a continuous monthly basis and remains subject to extensive regulatory and tax oversight.

In such circumstances, serious allegations such as tax fraud, suppression and persistent non-compliance should not be made casually or mechanically. These allegations carry significant legal and reputational consequences and must be supported by clear evidence. The impugned notice, however, does not identify any specific instance where tax was recovered by the Company and not deposited.

The Company respectfully submits that the impugned proceedings appear to have been initiated on a misunderstanding of the recovery-based mechanism applicable to DISCOs and without appreciating the prior compliance already made by the Company.

---

### 12. Without prejudice, the Company remains willing to re-submit and further reconcile the data

Without prejudice to the legal, factual and procedural objections raised hereinabove, and without admitting any default, the Company remains committed to full compliance with the Sales Tax Act, 1990, the Sales Tax Rules, 2006 and S.R.O. 376(I)/2023.

The Company is willing to re-submit the data already furnished earlier and to provide further reconciliation for the remaining period, if any, in a reasonable and mutually workable format. However, any such submission should not be treated as an admission of non-compliance, particularly where the Company has already complied to the extent permitted by IRIS and has already provided manual information when required.

The Company respectfully requests that the department may first share complete working of the figures mentioned in the impugned notice so that the same may be reconciled in a structured manner.

---

### Prayer

In view of the foregoing submissions, it is respectfully requested that:

a. the impugned show-cause notice dated 21 May 2026 issued for proposed blacklisting may kindly be withdrawn;  

b. the allegation of tax fraud, suppression and persistent violation may kindly be dropped, being contrary to facts, record and law;  

c. the suspension proceedings/order referred to in the impugned notice may also be reconsidered and withdrawn, as the matter is purely reconciliatory in nature;  

d. the prior compliance made through letter DST-1806 dated 17 June 2025 may kindly be taken on record;  

e. the department may kindly provide complete tax-period-wise and annexure-wise working of the figures referred to in the impugned notice; and  

f. in the alternative, if any further clarification or reconciliation is still required, reasonable time of at least fifteen days may kindly be allowed for submission of the same.

This reply is being submitted without prejudice to any other legal, factual, procedural or jurisdictional submissions which the Company may raise at any subsequent stage.

Yours faithfully,  

For and on behalf of  
**K-Electric Limited**  

_____________________  
Authorized Signatory  

**Enclosures:**  

1. Copy of letter DST-1806 dated 17 June 2025 along with acknowledgment.  
2. Copy of earlier reply dated 21 May 2026.  
3. Copy of FBR instructions C.No.6(4)Rev.Bud/2018 dated 23 July 2018.  
4. Relevant reconciliation/data already submitted earlier, where required.  
:::

I would slightly prefer this version over the earlier one because it now clearly separates the **procedural defect**, **factual defect**, **S.R.O. 376 mechanism**, **IRIS limitation**, **prior compliance**, and **absence of tax fraud**. This structure will help the Commissioner understand that the department’s action is not merely harsh, but legally and factually unsustainable.

We refer to Show Cause Notice C.No. CIR/Zone-VI/Suspension-ST/LTO/Khi/2025-26/348 dated May 21, 2026, issued under section 21(2A) of the Sales Tax Act, 1990 read with Rule 12(a)(vi) of the Sales Tax Rules, 2006, whereby K-Electric Limited [the “Company”] has been called upon to show cause as to why it may not be blacklisted on account of alleged persistent violation of the Sales Tax Act, 1990 read with S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 dated March 21, 2023.

At the outset, the Company respectfully denies the allegations contained in the impugned notice. The notice proceeds on an incorrect appreciation of facts, overlooks prior compliance already made by the Company, misconstrues the special recovery-based mechanism prescribed for DISCOs under S.R.O. 376(I)/2023, and seeks to invoke the extreme consequence of blacklisting without identifying any specific instance of deliberate suppression, false declaration, non-deposit of recovered tax, or tax fraud within the meaning of the Sales Tax Act, 1990.

The Company is a regulated electric power distribution company operating under a distinct commercial, regulatory and recovery framework. The difference between sales tax billed through electricity bills and sales tax actually recovered from consumers is an inherent feature of the DISCO recovery model and has been specifically recognized through S.R.O. 376(I)/2023. Such difference, by itself, cannot be equated with suppression of output tax or tax fraud.

**Background and Sequence of Proceedings**

The present notice appears to have been issued in continuation of earlier proceedings initiated through Show Cause Notice No. CIR/Zone-VI/LTO/Khi/2025-26/341 dated May 19, 2026, whereby the Company was called upon to explain why its sales tax registration should not be suspended under section 21(2) of the Sales Tax Act, 1990 read with Rule 12 of the Sales Tax Rules, 2006.

The earlier notice dated May 19, 2026 was premised primarily on an alleged decline in recovery ratio from 92.2% for the period June 2024 to February 2025 to 89.6% for the period June 2025 to February 2026. The allegation in the earlier notice was therefore confined to a comparative recovery-ratio observation for two limited periods.

The Company submitted its response to the said notice and explained that a marginal movement in recovery ratio could not, by itself, be treated as tax fraud or suppression of output tax. The Company also highlighted that the matter required reconciliation of voluminous billing, recovery and sales tax data and that the opportunity provided through the earlier notice was not reasonable or meaningful.

However, through the present blacklisting notice, the nature and scope of the allegation has been substantially altered. Instead of remaining confined to the recovery-ratio comparison referred to in the earlier notice, the present notice extends the tax periods to February 2023 to March 2026 and alleges that against total output sales tax billed of Rs. 326,567,252,303, the Company declared collection of Rs. 289,041,889,607.

This is not a mere continuation of the earlier proceedings. It is a materially expanded allegation based on a different period, different computation and different factual premise. A drastic action such as blacklisting cannot be founded upon shifting and enlarged allegations unless the precise basis, working, period-wise detail and supporting material are first provided to the taxpayer and a meaningful opportunity is allowed to respond.

The proceedings are therefore procedurally unfair, as the Company is being confronted with an enlarged allegation at the blacklisting stage without being provided the underlying computation and without being granted reasonable time to reconcile the same.

**Prior Compliance Ignored**

The allegation that the Company has failed to comply with S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 or failed to furnish requisite information is factually incorrect and contrary to the record.

In this regard, reference is invited to letter bearing reference DST-1806 dated June 17, 2025, submitted through the Company’s authorized representative in response to notice No. DCIR/U-4/Z-VI/LTO/S-147/2024-25/e-dox-11588 dated June 10, 2025. Through the said letter, the Company had already furnished complete information pertaining to overall movement, including recoveries and defaulting consumers, for the tax periods February 2023 to May 2025. A copy of letter DST-1806 dated June 17, 2025, along with acknowledgment, is enclosed herewith as Annexure ‘A’.

It is therefore evident that a substantial part of the very period now referred to in the impugned blacklisting notice had already been responded to by the Company. The relevant information had been furnished earlier and was available with the department. The impugned notice, however, proceeds on the assumption that no compliance was made, which is grossly incorrect.

Once the relevant data had already been provided for February 2023 to May 2025, the same could not have been ignored while alleging persistent non-compliance. At the very least, the department was required to examine the information already submitted, identify any specific deficiency therein, and allow the Company an opportunity to explain or supplement the same. Instead, the impugned notice proceeds directly towards blacklisting, which is neither justified nor sustainable.

It is further submitted that the Company has, from time to time and whenever required by the department, furnished detailed information relating to recovery of sales tax, including consumer-wise and record-wise details, in the manner requested by the concerned officers. Such information is not always capable of being reported through the standard fields available in the monthly sales tax return; however, as a responsible and compliant taxpayer, the Company has continued to provide the relevant data manually on an “as and when required” basis. Therefore, it is factually incorrect to allege that the Company has failed to furnish the requisite information or has not complied with the requirements of S.R.O. 376(I)/2023.

**IRIS Reporting Limitations**

The Company has been duly declaring relevant information in the monthly sales tax returns in the manner and to the extent permitted by the IRIS portal.

As already explained in earlier correspondence, the relevant annexure/tab in the sales tax return contains pre-defined fields. The IRIS portal does not provide an unrestricted facility for uploading detailed consumer-wise, party-wise or customized defaulting-consumer data beyond the system fields made available by FBR. A taxpayer cannot be expected to upload information in a format or field which the system itself does not provide.

This limitation is not attributable to the Company. It arises from the structure of the return and the system-based reporting mechanism. Therefore, the Company cannot be penalized or treated as non-compliant for not furnishing data in a manner which is not supported by the prescribed electronic return.

Where the IRIS system does not provide a specific facility for uploading detailed party-wise or consumer-wise information in the monthly sales tax return, no adverse inference can be drawn against the taxpayer for not furnishing such data electronically. If FBR requires any additional format, structured annexure or separate electronic filing facility for DISCOs under S.R.O. 376(I)/2023, the same may be prescribed and enabled formally. Until such mechanism is available, the taxpayer cannot be treated as non-compliant merely because the system does not allow the desired level of reporting.

This point was also explained in the earlier letter dated June 17, 2025. Despite this, the impugned notice shifts the entire burden of system limitation to the Company, which is neither fair nor sustainable.

**Billed Tax vs. Recovered Tax**

The principal assumption in the impugned notice appears to be that the difference between output sales tax billed and output sales tax recovered represents suppressed output tax. This assumption is legally and factually misconceived in the case of a DISCO operating under S.R.O. 376(I)/2023.

S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 was issued precisely to address the peculiar nature of the electric power distribution sector, where sales tax is billed to consumers through electricity bills, but actual realization depends upon subsequent recovery from consumers. The special procedure recognizes the distinction between billing and recovery and prescribes a mechanism for collection and payment accordingly.

In the electricity distribution sector, recoveries are affected by several factors, including delayed consumer payments, instalment arrangements, disputed bills, government receivables, category-wise consumer behavior, operational constraints, litigation, delayed realization and defaulting consumers. These factors are commercial and regulatory realities of the sector. They cannot be treated as evidence of suppression unless the department identifies a specific amount of tax that was actually recovered from consumers but not deposited by the Company.

The impugned notice does not identify any such amount. It does not point out any specific consumer, bill, receipt, tax period, return entry, bank recovery or collection record showing that sales tax was recovered by the Company but not deposited into the Government treasury. In the absence of such evidence, the difference between billed and recovered sales tax cannot be converted into an allegation of tax fraud.

Without prejudice to the Company’s legal objections, including the defective assumption of tax fraud, the factual incorrectness of the impugned notice, the absence of any specific allegation of tax actually recovered but not deposited, and the prior compliance already made for the period February 2023 to May 2025, it is respectfully submitted that the complete basis and working of the alleged differential amount of approximately Rs. 37.525 billion has not been provided. The impugned notice merely states aggregate figures of billed sales tax and recovered sales tax for the period February 2023 to March 2026, without providing tax-period-wise breakup, consumer/category-wise details, return-wise mapping, or identification of any amount allegedly recovered but not deposited. Since substantial details for February 2023 to May 2025 have already been furnished to the department, any remaining query, if at all, must be identified with precision so that the Company may reconcile and respond to the same in a meaningful manner.

**No Case for Blacklisting**

Blacklisting is an extraordinary and highly prejudicial action. It carries serious commercial, regulatory and reputational consequences and cannot be invoked merely because a reconciliation is required or because there is a difference between billed and recovered amounts under a special procedure.

The impugned notice alleges persistent violation and tax fraud. However, the essential ingredients of such allegation have not been established. The notice does not demonstrate that the Company has issued fake or false invoices, suppressed taxable supplies, recovered sales tax from consumers and failed to deposit the same, made false declarations in the sales tax returns, concealed any material record, failed to provide information despite reasonable and specific requisition, or deliberately violated any mandatory requirement of S.R.O. 376(I)/2023.

On the contrary, the record shows that the Company has been filing sales tax returns, reporting available information in the prescribed system fields, depositing recovered sales tax, responding to departmental notices, and furnishing manual data when called upon.

Therefore, the case does not fall within the scope of blacklisting. At most, the matter requires reconciliation of billed, recovered and unpaid amounts under the special procedure. Such reconciliation issue cannot be converted into proceedings for blacklisting.

**Responsible and Compliant Taxpayer**

The Company is one of the largest regulated taxpayers and contributors to the national exchequer. It collects and deposits substantial amounts of sales tax and withholding taxes on a continuous monthly basis and remains subject to extensive regulatory and tax oversight.

In such circumstances, serious allegations such as tax fraud, suppression and persistent non-compliance should not be made casually or mechanically. These allegations carry significant legal and reputational consequences and must be supported by clear evidence. The impugned notice, however, does not identify any specific instance where tax was recovered by the Company and not deposited.

The Company respectfully submits that the impugned proceedings appear to have been initiated on a misunderstanding of the recovery-based mechanism applicable to DISCOs and without appreciating the prior compliance already made by the Company.

**Conclusion**

In view of the above, the Company respectfully submits that the impugned notice is based on an incorrect appreciation of facts, an erroneous understanding of S.R.O. 376(I)/2023, and an unjustified assumption that the difference between billed and recovered sales tax constitutes tax fraud. The record clearly demonstrates that the Company has been filing its sales tax returns, declaring information to the extent permitted by IRIS, furnishing manual data whenever required, and has already submitted substantial information for the period February 2023 to May 2025.

Without prejudice to the foregoing legal and factual objections, and without admitting any default, the Company remains willing to re-submit the data already furnished earlier and to provide further reconciliation for the remaining period, if any, in a reasonable and mutually workable format. However, any further compliance must necessarily be preceded by provision of the complete tax-period-wise and annexure-wise working relied upon in the impugned notice, so that the matter may be reconciled on the basis of record rather than assumptions. In the circumstances, the proposed blacklisting is unwarranted and may kindly be dropped.

Such information is not always capable of being reported through the standard fields available in the monthly sales tax return; however, as a responsible and compliant taxpayer, the Company has continued to provide the relevant data manually on an “as and when required” basis. Therefore, it is factually incorrect to allege that the Company has failed to furnish the requisite information or has not complied with the requirements of S.R.O. 376(I)/2023.
IRIS REPORTING LIMITATIONS CANNOT BE TREATED AS NON-COMPLIANCE
The Company has been duly declaring relevant information in the monthly sales tax returns in the manner and to the extent permitted by the IRIS portal.
As already explained in earlier correspondence, the relevant annexure G in the sales tax return contains pre-defined fields. The IRIS portal does not provide an unrestricted facility for uploading detailed consumer-wise, party-wise or customized defaulting-consumer data beyond the system fields made available by FBR. A taxpayer cannot be expected to upload information in a format or field which the system itself does not provide.
This limitation is not attributable to the Company. It arises from the structure of the return and the system-based reporting mechanism. Therefore, the Company cannot be penalized or treated as non-compliant for not furnishing data in a manner which is not supported by the prescribed electronic return.
Where the IRIS system does not provide a specific facility for uploading detailed party-wise or consumer-wise information in the monthly sales tax return, no adverse inference can be drawn against the taxpayer for not furnishing such data electronically. If FBR requires any additional format, structured annexure or separate electronic filing facility for DISCOs under S.R.O. 376(I)/2023, the same may be prescribed and enabled formally. Until such mechanism is available, the taxpayer cannot be treated as non-compliant merely because the system does not allow the desired level of reporting.
This point was also explained in the earlier letter dated June 17, 2025. Despite this, the impugned notice shifts the entire burden of system limitation to the Company, which is neither fair nor sustainable.
BILLED TAX VS. RECOVERED TAX
The principal assumption in the impugned notice appears to be that the difference between output sales tax billed and output sales tax recovered represents suppressed output tax. This assumption is legally and factually misconceived in the case of a DISCO operating under S.R.O. 376(I)/2023.
S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 was issued precisely to address the peculiar nature of the electric power distribution sector, where sales tax is billed to consumers through electricity bills, but actual realization depends upon subsequent recovery from consumers. The special procedure recognizes the distinction between billing and recovery and prescribes a mechanism for collection and payment accordingly.
In the electricity distribution sector, recoveries are affected by several factors, including delayed consumer payments, instalment arrangements, disputed bills, government receivables, category-wise consumer behavior, operational constraints, litigation, delayed realization and defaulting consumers. These factors are commercial and regulatory realities of the sector. They cannot be treated as evidence of suppression unless the department identifies a specific amount of tax that was actually recovered from consumers but not deposited by the Company.
The impugned notice does not identify any such amount. It does not point out any specific consumer, bill, receipt, tax period, return entry, bank recovery or collection record showing that sales tax was recovered by the Company but not deposited into the Government treasury. In the absence of such evidence, the difference between billed and recovered sales tax cannot be converted into an allegation of tax fraud.
Without prejudice to the Company’s legal objections, including the defective assumption of tax fraud, the factual incorrectness of the impugned notice, the absence of any specific allegation of tax actually recovered but not deposited, and the prior compliance already made for the period February 2023 to May 2025, it is respectfully submitted that the complete details of the alleged differential amount of approximately Rs. 37.525 billion is enclosed as Annexure ‘B’, for your perusal.  
NO CASE FOR BLACKLISTING
Blacklisting is an extraordinary and highly prejudicial action. It carries serious commercial, regulatory and reputational consequences and cannot be invoked merely because a reconciliation is required or because there is a difference between billed and recovered amounts under a special procedure.
The impugned notice alleges persistent violation and tax fraud. However, the essential ingredients of such allegation have not been established. The notice does not demonstrate that the Company has issued fake or false invoices, suppressed taxable supplies, recovered sales tax from consumers and failed to deposit the same, made false declarations in the sales tax returns, concealed any material record, failed to provide information despite reasonable and specific requisition, or deliberately violated any mandatory requirement of S.R.O. 376(I)/2023.
On the contrary, the record shows that the Company has been filing sales tax returns, reporting available information in the prescribed system fields, depositing recovered sales tax, responding to departmental notices, and furnishing manual data when called upon.
Therefore, the case does not fall within the scope of blacklisting. At most, the matter requires reconciliation of billed, recovered and unpaid amounts under the special procedure. Such reconciliation issue cannot be converted into proceedings for blacklisting.
RESPONSIBLE AND COMPLIANT TAXPAYER
The Company is one of the largest regulated taxpayers and contributors to the national exchequer. It collects and deposits substantial amounts of sales tax and withholding taxes on a continuous monthly basis and remains subject to extensive regulatory and tax oversight.
In such circumstances, serious allegations such as tax fraud, suppression and persistent non-compliance should not be made casually or mechanically. These allegations carry significant legal and reputational consequences and must be supported by clear evidence. The impugned notice, however, does not identify any specific instance where tax was recovered by the Company and not deposited.
The Company respectfully submits that the impugned proceedings appear to have been initiated on a misunderstanding of the recovery-based mechanism applicable to DISCOs and without appreciating the prior compliance already made by the Company.

We refer to Show Cause Notice C.No. CIR/Zone-VI/Suspension-ST/LTO/Khi/2025-26/348 dated May 21, 2026, issued under section 21(2A) of the Sales Tax Act, 1990 read with Rule 12(a)(vi) of the Sales Tax Rules, 2006, whereby K-Electric Limited [the “Company”] has been called upon to show cause as to why it may not be blacklisted on account of alleged persistent violation of the Sales Tax Act, 1990 read with S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 dated March 21, 2023.

At the outset, the Company respectfully denies the allegations contained in the impugned notice. The notice proceeds on an incorrect appreciation of facts, overlooks prior compliance already made by the Company, misconstrues the special recovery-based mechanism prescribed for DISCOs under S.R.O. 376(I)/2023, and seeks to invoke the extreme consequence of blacklisting without identifying any specific instance of deliberate suppression, false declaration, non-deposit of recovered tax, or tax fraud within the meaning of the Sales Tax Act, 1990.

The Company is a regulated electric power distribution company operating under a distinct commercial, regulatory and recovery framework. The difference between sales tax billed through electricity bills and sales tax actually recovered from consumers is an inherent feature of the DISCO recovery model and has been specifically recognized through S.R.O. 376(I)/2023. Such difference, by itself, cannot be equated with suppression of output tax or tax fraud.

**Background: Earlier Notice Was Based on a Limited Recovery-Ratio Observation**

The instant notice appears to have been issued in continuation of earlier proceedings initiated through Show Cause Notice No. CIR/Zone-VI/LTO/Khi/2025-26/341 dated May 19, 2026, whereby the Company was called upon to explain why its sales tax registration should not be suspended under section 21(2) of the Sales Tax Act, 1990 read with Rule 12 of the Sales Tax Rules, 2006.

The earlier notice was premised primarily on an alleged decline in recovery ratio from 92.2% for the period June 2024 to February 2025 to 89.6% for the period June 2025 to February 2026. The Company duly responded and explained that a marginal movement in recovery ratio could not, by itself, be treated as suppression of output tax or tax fraud. The Company also highlighted that the matter involved reconciliation of voluminous billing, recovery and sales tax data and that the time allowed was not reasonable or meaningful.

Through the present blacklisting notice, however, the nature and scope of the allegation has been substantially altered. Instead of remaining confined to the recovery-ratio comparison referred to in the earlier notice, the present notice extends the tax periods to February 2023 to March 2026 and alleges that against total output sales tax billed of Rs. 326,567,252,303, the Company declared collection of Rs. 289,041,889,607.

This is not a mere continuation of the earlier proceedings. It is a materially expanded allegation based on a different period, different computation and different factual premise. A drastic action such as blacklisting cannot be founded upon shifting and enlarged allegations unless the precise basis, working, period-wise detail and supporting material are first provided to the taxpayer and a meaningful opportunity is allowed to respond.

**Prior Compliance and Information Already Furnished**

The allegation that the Company has failed to comply with S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 or failed to furnish requisite information is factually incorrect and contrary to the record.

In this regard, reference is invited to letter bearing reference DST-1806 dated June 17, 2025, submitted through the Company’s authorized representative in response to notice No. DCIR/U-4/Z-VI/LTO/S-147/2024-25/e-dox-11588 dated June 10, 2025. Through the said letter, the Company had already furnished complete information pertaining to overall movement, including recoveries and defaulting consumers, for the tax periods February 2023 to May 2025. A copy of the said letter, along with acknowledgment, is enclosed herewith as Annexure ‘A’.

It is therefore evident that a substantial part of the very period now referred to in the impugned blacklisting notice had already been responded to by the Company and the relevant information was available with the department. Once the said data had already been provided, the same could not have been ignored while alleging persistent non-compliance. At the very least, the department was required to examine the information already submitted, identify any specific deficiency therein, and allow the Company an opportunity to explain or supplement the same.

It is further submitted that the Company has, from time to time and whenever required by the department, furnished detailed information relating to recovery of sales tax, including consumer-wise and record-wise details, in the manner requested by the concerned officers. Such information is not always capable of being reported through the standard fields available in the monthly sales tax return; however, as a responsible and compliant taxpayer, the Company has continued to provide the relevant data manually on an “as and when required” basis.

**IRIS Reporting Limitation Is Not Non-Compliance**

The Company has been duly declaring relevant information in the monthly sales tax returns in the manner and to the extent permitted by the IRIS portal. As already explained in earlier correspondence, the relevant Annexure G in the sales tax return contains pre-defined fields and does not provide an unrestricted facility for uploading detailed consumer-wise, party-wise or customized defaulting-consumer data beyond the system fields made available by FBR.

This limitation is not attributable to the Company. It arises from the structure of the return and the system-based reporting mechanism. A taxpayer cannot be expected to upload information in a format or field which the system itself does not provide. If FBR requires any additional format, structured annexure or separate electronic filing facility for DISCOs under S.R.O. 376(I)/2023, the same may be prescribed and enabled formally. Until such mechanism is available, the taxpayer cannot be treated as non-compliant merely because the system does not allow the desired level of reporting.

**Billed Tax and Recovered Tax Are Distinct Under the DISCO Mechanism**

The principal assumption in the impugned notice appears to be that the difference between output sales tax billed and output sales tax recovered represents suppressed output tax. This assumption is legally and factually misconceived in the case of a DISCO operating under S.R.O. 376(I)/2023.

S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 was issued precisely to address the peculiar nature of the electric power distribution sector, where sales tax is billed to consumers through electricity bills, but actual realization depends upon subsequent recovery from consumers. Recoveries are affected by delayed consumer payments, instalment arrangements, disputed bills, government receivables, category-wise consumer behavior, operational constraints, litigation, delayed realization and defaulting consumers. These are commercial and regulatory realities of the sector and cannot be treated as evidence of suppression unless the department identifies a specific amount of tax that was actually recovered from consumers but not deposited by the Company.

The impugned notice does not identify any such amount. It does not point out any specific consumer, bill, receipt, tax period, return entry, bank recovery or collection record showing that sales tax was recovered by the Company but not deposited into the Government treasury. In the absence of such evidence, the difference between billed and recovered sales tax cannot be converted into an allegation of tax fraud.

Without prejudice to the Company’s legal objections, including the defective assumption of tax fraud, factual incorrectness of the impugned notice, absence of any specific allegation of tax actually recovered but not deposited, and prior compliance already made for the period February 2023 to May 2025, the details of the alleged differential amount of approximately Rs. 37.525 billion are enclosed as Annexure ‘B’ for your perusal.

**No Statutory Basis for Blacklisting**

Blacklisting is an extraordinary and highly prejudicial action carrying serious commercial, regulatory and reputational consequences. Such action cannot be invoked merely because a reconciliation is required or because there is a difference between billed and recovered amounts under a special procedure.

The impugned notice alleges persistent violation and tax fraud; however, the essential ingredients of such allegation have not been established. The notice does not demonstrate that the Company has issued fake or false invoices, suppressed taxable supplies, recovered sales tax from consumers and failed to deposit the same, made false declarations in sales tax returns, concealed any material record, failed to provide information despite reasonable and specific requisition, or deliberately violated any mandatory requirement of S.R.O. 376(I)/2023.

On the contrary, the record shows that the Company has been filing sales tax returns, reporting available information in the prescribed system fields, depositing recovered sales tax, responding to departmental notices, and furnishing manual data when called upon. At most, the matter requires reconciliation of billed, recovered and unpaid amounts under the special procedure. Such reconciliation issue cannot be converted into proceedings for blacklisting.

**Conclusion**

In view of the above, the Company respectfully submits that the impugned notice is based on an incorrect appreciation of facts, an erroneous understanding of S.R.O. 376(I)/2023, and an unjustified assumption that the difference between billed and recovered sales tax constitutes tax fraud. The record clearly demonstrates that the Company has been filing its sales tax returns, declaring information to the extent permitted by IRIS, furnishing manual data whenever required, and has already submitted substantial information for the period February 2023 to May 2025.

The Company is one of the largest regulated taxpayers and contributors to the national exchequer and remains committed to full compliance with the Sales Tax Act, 1990, the Sales Tax Rules, 2006 and S.R.O. 376(I)/2023. In the circumstances, the proposed blacklisting is unwarranted and may kindly be dropped. Without prejudice, the Company remains available to assist the department in any further reconciliation, if required, in a reasonable and mutually workable manner.

I have critically reviewed all three documents: the first suspension show-cause notice dated **19 May 2026**, K-Electric’s reply dated **21 May 2026** fileciteturn0file0, and the subsequent blacklisting show-cause notice dated **21 May 2026** fileciteturn0file1. The overall position appears to be that the department first initiated suspension proceedings on the basis of alleged non-compliance with S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 and alleged decline in recovery ratio, while K-Electric responded mainly on the grounds of inadequate opportunity, absence of proper verification, and the harshness of suspension. Thereafter, instead of first addressing the reply or allowing reasonable time for reconciliation, the department has escalated the matter by issuing a blacklisting show-cause notice.

### Critical reading of the first notice dated 19 May 2026

The first notice alleges non-compliance with S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 on the basis that the recovery ratio declined from **92.2%** during June 2024 to February 2025 to **89.6%** during June 2025 to February 2026. The department treats this movement as a “material decline” and then links it with alleged unverifiable recoveries, suppression of output tax and reduction of sales tax liability.

In my view, this is a weak foundation for suspension proceedings. A movement from 92.2% to 89.6% is a variation of around **2.6 percentage points**, and in the case of an electricity distribution company, recovery ratios naturally fluctuate due to billing cycles, consumer mix, government receivables, delayed payments, seasonal consumption patterns, industrial/commercial load variation, and category-wise recovery trends. Merely comparing two broad periods and concluding “tax fraud” is not legally sustainable unless the officer first identifies specific transactions, invoices, billing records, recovery data, or return entries which are false, suppressed or materially unverifiable.

Another important defect is that the notice fixed hearing on **20 May 2026**, i.e. the very next day after issuance on **19 May 2026**. Since the notice sought reconciliation over multiple periods and required voluminous data relating to billing, recovery and sales tax, this short timeline seriously affects the taxpayer’s right of proper opportunity. K-Electric’s reply correctly relied on FBR’s own instructions requiring sufficient time/fair opportunity of at least fifteen days before compliance fileciteturn0file0.

### Critical reading of K-Electric’s reply dated 21 May 2026

The reply is directionally correct and professionally positioned. It raises three strong points: first, that the opportunity was unreasonable; second, that a marginal decline in recovery ratio cannot by itself constitute tax fraud; and third, that suspension is an extremely harsh action where the issue essentially relates to reconciliation and verification of billing/recovery data.

However, the reply is more defensive and procedural in nature. It does not appear to annex or offer a structured reconciliation at this stage. From a litigation perspective, that is understandable because the time given was only one day. However, now that the department has escalated the matter to blacklisting, the next response should not remain limited to opportunity and hardship. It should include a stronger factual rebuttal, preferably with annexures showing the exact reconciliation of billed sales tax, recovered sales tax, unpaid/defaulted amount, government receivables, delayed recoveries, and the manner in which S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 is being complied with.

The reply rightly states that the Company is a regulated electric power utility and that billing/recovery mechanisms are subject to regulatory, commercial and operational controls fileciteturn0file0. This point should now be expanded in detail. The department’s allegation of “tax fraud” must be confronted directly by explaining that a DISCO’s recovery-based sales tax mechanism under S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 is not equivalent to suppression of sales; rather, it recognizes the practical difference between billed amount and actual recovered amount.

### Critical reading of the blacklisting show-cause notice dated 21 May 2026

The blacklisting notice is more serious. It refers to an earlier suspension order dated **20 May 2026** and states that sales tax registration has already been suspended. The notice then proposes blacklisting under **section 21(2A)** read with **Rule 12(a)(vi)** on the ground of alleged tax fraud and persistent violation of S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 fileciteturn0file1.

The department has also introduced a much larger allegation for the period **February 2023 to March 2026**, stating that against total output sales tax billed of **Rs. 326,567,252,303**, K-Electric declared collection of only **Rs. 289,041,889,607** fileciteturn0file1. This means the alleged differential is approximately **Rs. 37.525 billion**. This is now materially different from the first notice, which was mainly based on a comparative recovery ratio for two periods. Therefore, one key argument will be that the blacklisting notice materially enlarges the controversy and introduces a fresh basis without first providing proper working, transaction-level details, annexures, or reconciliation format to allow the taxpayer to respond meaningfully.

There is also an apparent procedural concern. The department issued the first show-cause notice on **19 May 2026**, fixed hearing on **20 May 2026**, proceeded to suspension, and then issued blacklisting show-cause notice on **21 May 2026**. This rapid sequence can be challenged as a mechanical escalation without proper consideration of K-Electric’s reply dated 21 May 2026. The principle point is that if the taxpayer had already requested reasonable time and had pointed out the need for reconciliation, the department should have first allowed proper opportunity before invoking the extreme consequence of blacklisting.

### Key legal and factual weaknesses in department’s case

The department appears to be treating **unrecovered billed sales tax** as if it were automatically suppressed output tax. That approach is not correct in the context of S.R.O. 376(I)/2023. The whole purpose of the special procedure is to deal with the peculiar recovery model of DISCOs and to regulate the collection/payment of sales tax based on actual recoveries, along with reporting of unpaid/defaulted amounts. Therefore, the department must distinguish between:

1. sales tax billed but not yet recovered from consumers;  
2. sales tax actually recovered and deposited;  
3. unpaid/defaulted amounts reported under the prescribed annexures;  
4. permanent defaulters, if any, dealt with under the special procedure; and  
5. any actual case of misdeclaration or suppression.

Without this distinction, the allegation of tax fraud is premature and legally vulnerable.

The second weakness is absence of transaction-wise or consumer-category-wise analysis. A figure of Rs. 326.567 billion billed versus Rs. 289.042 billion recovered may show an unrecovered component, but it does not automatically prove tax fraud. For blacklisting, the department must show intentional suppression, false declaration, fake documentation, or deliberate short payment. A recovery gap, by itself, is a commercial/regulatory phenomenon unless linked with specific concealment.

The third weakness is denial of adequate opportunity. The department’s own earlier instructions requiring reasonable time are directly helpful. Since the matter involves more than three years of data, a compliance date of **25 May 2026** in the blacklisting notice is still very short, especially after suspension has already been made.

### Recommended response strategy

The next reply should be stronger than the earlier letter. It should not merely request withdrawal or extension. It should ask the Commissioner to first recall/withdraw the suspension and drop blacklisting proceedings, or at minimum keep coercive action in abeyance, because the matter is purely reconciliatory and cannot be branded as tax fraud without proper verification.

The reply should include a chronology:

**19 May 2026:** first show-cause notice issued.  
**20 May 2026:** hearing fixed on the very next day.  
**21 May 2026:** K-Electric submitted reply requesting withdrawal/reasonable time.  
**20/21 May 2026:** suspension/blacklisting process initiated without meaningful consideration of reply.  
**25 May 2026:** compliance fixed for blacklisting despite voluminous data covering February 2023 to March 2026.

The reply should also demand the detailed working behind the alleged figure of Rs. 37.525 billion, including tax period-wise, consumer category-wise, and annexure-wise basis, because without that working K-Electric cannot be expected to give a meaningful rebuttal.

Most importantly, K-Electric should now prepare a reconciliation pack. Even if full reconciliation is not immediately ready, the response should state that the Company is compiling period-wise data and is willing to submit it in phases. This will demonstrate bona fide compliance and weaken the department’s allegation of deliberate suppression.

### Practical documents/data now required

For the next response, the following should be immediately compiled:

- Month-wise output sales tax billed from February 2023 to March 2026.  
- Month-wise output sales tax recovered and deposited.  
- Month-wise unpaid/defaulted sales tax balance.  
- Annex-A or relevant S.R.O. 376(I)/2023 reporting submitted with returns.  
- Category-wise recovery breakup, if available.  
- Government department receivables, delayed recovery, disputed billing, and permanently disconnected/defaulted consumers.  
- Sales tax return extracts supporting declared recovered amounts.  
- PSIDs/CPRs evidencing payment of recovered sales tax.  
- Explanation of recovery-based mechanism under S.R.O. 376(I)/2023.

### Bottom line

The department’s escalation from suspension to blacklisting appears premature, harsh and procedurally vulnerable. The strongest defence is that this is not a case of tax fraud; it is, at highest, a reconciliation issue arising from the special recovery-based sales tax mechanism applicable to DISCOs. The next reply should combine procedural objections with factual reconciliation and should specifically challenge the assumption that unrecovered billed tax is equivalent to suppressed output tax.

Below is a more refined and legally aligned version of the notice. I have retained the proposed 10% computation as given, but please verify the applicable withholding section and rate before issuance, particularly whether the payment falls under **section 151 “profit on debt”** or any other withholding provision applicable to the transaction. Under FBR’s withholding framework, a withholding agent may be held personally liable where tax was required to be deducted but was not deducted, or was deducted but not paid to the Federal Government. citeturn176106search18

---

**SHOW CAUSE NOTICE / OPPORTUNITY OF BEING HEARD UNDER SECTION 161 READ WITH SECTION 161(1A) OF THE INCOME TAX ORDINANCE, 2001 FOR TAX YEAR 2027**

Please refer to the subject cited above.

On examination of the available record, it has been observed that an amount of **Rs. 7,253,811,000** has accrued / been credited / paid to **M/s Gold Trade International Limited** on account of interest / profit pertaining to working capital facilities and long-term loans during the relevant tax year. However, no evidence is available on record to establish that tax was duly deducted and deposited, as required under the relevant withholding provisions of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001.

In view of the foregoing, it appears that you, being the person responsible for deduction of tax at source, have failed to deduct and / or deposit withholding tax on the aforesaid amount. Accordingly, you are hereby required to show cause as to why proceedings may not be finalized under **section 161 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001**, and why an amount of **Rs. 725,381,100**, calculated at the rate of **10%** on **Rs. 7,253,811,000**, may not be recovered from you as tax not deducted / not paid, along with default surcharge under **section 161(1A)** of the Ordinance, where applicable.

You are, therefore, afforded an opportunity of being heard and are required to furnish your written explanation, along with all relevant documentary evidence, including but not limited to loan agreements, ledger accounts, details of interest accrued / paid, withholding tax challans / CPRs, tax deduction certificates, reconciliations and any other supporting record, on or before the due date fixed for compliance.

Please note that in case of non-compliance, or where the explanation furnished is found unsatisfactory, the proceedings shall be finalized on the basis of available record, in accordance with the provisions of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 and the facts of the case.

---

parts: اچھا اس پر ذرا ڈیپ ریسرچ کریں کہ سیلز ٹیکس ایکٹ کی جو ایکٹو ٹیکس پر لسٹ ہے وہ کب اپ ڈیٹ ہوتی ہے وہ ریئل ٹائم اپڈیٹ ہوتی ہے یا کوئی ٹائم فریم ہے اس کا

Based on FBR’s own material, **Sales Tax ATL / Active Taxpayer List (ST) does not appear to be officially confirmed as “real-time” in the same way we often assume from the online search utility.** The more defensible position is:

**FBR maintains an online Sales Tax ATL database and also publishes a downloadable Sales Tax ATL file from time to time. The downloadable file is clearly batch-updated, while the online verification utility may reflect the database more promptly, but FBR’s public Sales Tax ATL page does not state that it is updated instantly or in real time.**

### Key findings

FBR describes the **Sales Tax Active Taxpayer List** as “a central record of online active Sales Tax Return filers.” This means it is tied to sales tax registration/return compliance and status in FBR’s system, not merely to income tax filer status. citeturn381050view0

For **Sales Tax ATL inclusion**, FBR says the person must be registered and must not fall into the following categories: blacklisted/suspended/blocked, failure to file sales tax return by due date for two consecutive tax periods, failure to file income tax return by due date, or failure to file two consecutive monthly/annual withholding statements. citeturn147194view0

FBR’s **downloadable Sales Tax ATL page** shows the list as “Updated on” a specific date — for example, the page I accessed shows “Active Taxpayer List (Sales Tax) – Updated on 06 Apr 2026.” That wording strongly indicates a **periodic/batch publication**, not a continuously real-time downloadable list. citeturn381050view1

By contrast, FBR’s **Income Tax ATL page expressly says** that the income tax ATL is updated every Monday. The Sales Tax ATL page does **not** contain a similar clear weekly/daily update statement. This distinction is important: we should not automatically apply the income tax ATL Monday-update rule to Sales Tax ATL unless FBR expressly provides it for Sales Tax as well. citeturn627133view0

### Practical conclusion

For advisory purposes, I would frame it as follows:

> The Sales Tax ATL is not officially described by FBR as a real-time list. The downloadable ATL (ST) file is updated periodically and carries a specific “updated on” date. However, the online ATL status check is the more current verification source and should be used for transaction-date verification, especially where input tax admissibility, supplier status, suspension, or blacklisting exposure is involved.

### Important compliance angle

Where a person is **suspended**, FBR states that input tax adjustment/refund is not available to the suspended person, and no input tax adjustment/refund is allowed to other registered persons on the basis of invoices issued by such suspended person, whether issued before or after suspension. citeturn147194view1

So in practice, for any sensitive transaction, I would recommend:

1. Check the supplier/customer status through the **online Sales Tax ATL verification utility** on the relevant date.
2. Save screenshot/PDF evidence showing NTN/CNIC, date, time, and status.
3. Do not rely only on the downloaded ATL file if the matter involves input tax claim, suspension, blacklisting, or departmental challenge.
4. If status recently changed after return filing or restoration, allow for system/batch processing lag and obtain confirmation through IRIS/profile/status screen or FBR online verification.

### My professional view

If a client asks whether it is “real time,” the safe answer is:

**No official public source confirms that Sales Tax ATL is updated on a real-time basis. The downloadable Sales Tax ATL is clearly date-based/batch-updated. The online status check may be more current, but for legal/compliance purposes it should be treated as system-based verification rather than guaranteed real-time updating.**

Based on the SRB hearing notice dated **09.05.2026** and your earlier reply dated **06.05.2026**, I have drafted the continuation reply below. fileciteturn0file0 fileciteturn1file0

:::writing{variant="standard" id="48291"}
**Date:** May 21, 2026  

**Ms. Sadia Adeel**  
Assistant Commissioner (Unit-04)  
Sindh Revenue Board  
2nd Floor, Shaheen Complex  
M. R. Kiyani Road  
Karachi  

**Respected Madam,**  

### **M/s Mir Associates**  
### **Submission of Additional Supporting Documents and Request for Further Time in Continuation of Hearing Notice No. SRB-COM-VII/AC-04/2025-26/795033 dated May 09, 2026 issued in relation to Show Cause Notice No. 706701 dated November 28, 2025**

We refer to Hearing Notice No. **SRB-COM-VII/AC-04/2025-26/795033 dated May 09, 2026**, issued in relation to Show Cause Notice No. **706701 dated November 28, 2025**, whereby your good office has been pleased to communicate that our request for extension in time has been considered and the next date of hearing has been fixed for **May 21, 2026 at 11:30 A.M.**

At the outset, we respectfully thank your good office for considering our request for extension and for allowing further opportunity to submit the relevant record and explanations in support of our position. We remain fully committed to assisting your good office in proper reconciliation of the matter on the basis of actual invoices, customer payment evidence and verifiable records.

In continuation of our earlier submission dated **May 06, 2026**, it is respectfully submitted that during the earlier hearing and through our written response, we had highlighted that certain entries/invoices appearing in the details forming basis of the proceedings require correction, as in some cases the amount representing the taxable value/service value appears to have been incorrectly captured as Sindh Sales Tax amount. This has resulted in an overstated position, since the gross value of services and the amount of Sindh Sales Tax cannot be treated as one and the same.

One of the major invoices identified in this respect relates to **M/s Shan Foods**, involving an amount of approximately **Rs. 12 million**. Through the present letter, we are submitting the relevant supporting documents in respect of the said transaction, which clearly establish that the amount of **Rs. 12 million represented the gross service value/taxable value of the transaction and not the amount of Sindh Sales Tax**.

In support of the above position, we are enclosing herewith the following documents for your kind examination:

**Annexure ‘A’** – Copy of relevant invoice issued by M/s Mir Associates;  
**Annexure ‘B’** – Copy of purchase order / relevant customer document issued by M/s Shan Foods;  
**Annexure ‘C’** – Copy of payment advice / payment support received from M/s Shan Foods; and  
**Annexure ‘D’** – Relevant extract of bank statement evidencing receipt of payment.

On perusal of the enclosed documents, it would be evident that the amount of approximately **Rs. 12 million was the gross value of services**. Further, the payment evidence also reflects that applicable deductions/withholdings were made from the gross amount, including withholding of Sindh Sales Tax and income tax, where applicable. Accordingly, the said amount cannot, under any circumstances, be treated as the amount of Sindh Sales Tax. Treating the gross service value itself as sales tax would result in an incorrect and excessive computation, which is not supported by the underlying invoice, payment record or banking evidence.

We therefore respectfully request your good office to kindly examine the enclosed documents and correct the said entry in the working accordingly. The transaction may kindly be reconciled by treating the amount of approximately **Rs. 12 million as the gross/taxable value of services**, and not as the amount of Sindh Sales Tax.

It is further submitted that certain remaining factual and legal explanations, along with supporting documents in respect of other entries, are still under compilation. The matter requires coordination with customers and retrieval of relevant internal records, including invoices, payment details and reconciliations. Therefore, while we are submitting the presently available record through this letter, we respectfully request that further time of at least **fifteen days** may kindly be allowed for submission of the remaining explanations and supporting documents.

In view of the above, the enclosed documents may kindly be taken on record and considered before drawing any adverse inference in the matter. In case any further clarification, reconciliation or supporting evidence is required from our side, the same may kindly be intimated so that it may be submitted accordingly.

We trust that the above submissions and enclosed documents will be considered in their proper perspective, and the impugned discrepancy will be corrected on the basis of actual documentary evidence.

**Yours faithfully,**  

For and on behalf of  
**M/s Mir Associates**  
:::
